# GEO report: ledger-site **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 72/100, Good Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. The basics are mostly in place, but a few fixable gaps cost points. The page language isn't declared, `robots.txt` doesn't point to your sitemap, and two pages have no canonical. No rule came out as Can't tell. Every result is read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Declare the page language - **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells browsers and machines which language the site is in. Without it they have to guess. - **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Change it to ``, matching `site.language` in `geo.config.json`. - **Score after this:** 80/100 ### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap - **Why it matters:** A sitemap is your list of pages. `robots.txt` is where crawlers look first, and it doesn't link to the list. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`. The file has no `Sitemap:` line, even though `public/sitemap.xml` exists. - **What the code says:** `Allow: /` is the last rule for `*`, and nothing follows it except the GPTBot group. - **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`. - **Score after this:** 80/100. Doing items 1 and 2 together gives 18.5 + 2 = 20.5 ÷ 23 = 89. ### 3. Add a canonical link to /docs and /blog - **Why it matters:** A canonical link names the main address of a page, so search engines don't have to choose between duplicate addresses. Your home and pricing pages have one, but these two don't. - **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`. `app/blog/page.tsx` has no metadata at all, and the layout sets no canonical. - **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 76/100 on its own. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines, tiny | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can access the site as your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` (`User-agent: *` / `Allow: /`) | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/pricing` is noindex (`app/pricing/page.tsx:1`). 3 of 4 routes are clear: 3 × 3/4 = 2.25 | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Problem | Not run | `/docs` and `/blog` have none (`app/docs/page.tsx:1`). 2 of 4 routes are clear: 2 × 2/4 = 1 | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7-9`. 3 of 4 routes are clear: 3 × 3/4 = 2.25 | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line, though `public/sitemap.xml` is valid | | GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11`. Title and description are present on every route, but `lang` is missing site-wide | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has `` links to all four pages | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` anywhere. `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:15` is a deliberate, scoped choice | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and all 5 pages. There are no images, and links and buttons have text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | Not run | None present | ## Other problems found - **Pricing is noindex but listed in the sitemap and the menu:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. The sitemap (`public/sitemap.xml:4`) and nav (`app/layout.tsx:13`) both promote it, and its canonical points to itself. Remove `robots: { index: false ... }` if the page should be found. Otherwise remove it from the sitemap. ## Worth considering - **Your training-crawler policy is only partly applied:** `geo.config.json`: `"trainingCrawlers": "block"`, but `public/robots.txt:4-5` names only `GPTBot`. If you want the policy applied fully, add groups for the other training crawlers you intend to block, such as `ClaudeBot`. - **Blog posts have no pages of their own:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `
{p.title}
`. Each post could get its own address and a link from the blog list. That would give crawlers pages to find and quote, and server rendering would show the titles in the first HTML. - **Pricing says very little in text:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `

Free for up to three people.

`. The meta description promises "Plans for every team size", but no other plans are described. Writing the plans and prices as text might help readers and machines. - **Docs is a single sentence:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `

Start by importing your bank feed.

`. The page title is "Docs" and the description is "How to set up Ledger.", but there are no setup steps. Adding them as text would deliver on that promise. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Live-only checks:** whether the sitemap URLs and canonical targets answer 200, and whether `/api/posts` is served. A live scan would confirm these. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in your config. - `/thank-you` is deliberately noindex and is not in the sitemap or menu, so I didn't count it. - I sampled all four public routes, which is every page in the sitemap. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
